title: Fine-tuning a pretrained model, and which layers to freeze

videos.script: Lesson 13 borrowed a trained network and kept it frozen. This lesson lets it learn. {{recap}} The question is how much of it. Only a new head, the last block as well, or every layer. {{depths}} In PyTorch, each choice is one flag on each tensor, and a list handed to the optimiser. {{flags}} You will try all three on the digits 5 to 9, against a network trained from scratch. {{table}} The answer is honest, and not flattering. The more of the body learns, the better it does. And scratch still wins. {{result}} Then the learning rate. It decides how far the weights travel from what you borrowed. {{rates}} Travel far enough and the old digits are gone. At the highest rate, 0 to 4 fell from almost perfect to under a third. {{forget}} LoRA keeps the old weights frozen, and learns a thin correction beside them. {{lora}} It matched the last block with about a twelfth of the parameters. Take it off, and the old task is back, exactly. {{restore}} Last, the same decisions on a language model with seven billion weights. There they decide whether training fits at all. {{scale}} That part is counted here, and not run. {{end}}
